prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Conservatives’ plan is to secure Britain’s future by sticking with the approach that has brought inflation down, real wages up and growth back—while cutting taxes, controlling immigration, strengthening defence and improving public services. The alternative is Labour’s higher taxes, looser borders and economic risk.

- Backing work and family finances: Halve employee National Insurance to 6% by 2027; abolish main self‑employed NI next Parliament; Triple Lock Plus so both the State Pension and pensioner tax‑free allowance always rise by at least inflation, earnings or 2.5%; 30 hours’ free childcare from 9 months; fairer Child Benefit on a household basis starting at £120,000; no new green levies.

- Pro‑growth economy: No rise in corporation tax; expand full expensing (incl. leasing when affordable); a 10‑point SME plan; cut EU red tape using Brexit freedoms; nationwide gigabit by 2030 and standalone 5G; £22bn a year public R&D; advanced manufacturing push; keep the City globally competitive; more trade deals (CPTPP in, India/GCC next) without surrendering sovereignty.

- Welfare that’s fair and makes work pay: Reform disability benefits and fit notes; tighten work capability assessments; tougher sanctions at 12 months; accelerate Universal Credit rollout; zero‑tolerance on fraud; continued support for unpaid carers.

- Opportunity for the next generation: Advanced British Standard to end the academic/technical divide; 100,000 more high‑quality apprenticeships funded by closing poor‑value degrees; statutory school‑day mobile phone ban; parents’ clear right to see what’s taught; modern National Service (competitive paid military year or civic service one‑weekend‑a‑month).

- Borders and security: A binding legal cap to bring migration down every year; higher salary thresholds and fewer dependants; monthly removals to Rwanda to stop the boats; rewrite asylum treaties; defence spending to 2.5% of GDP by 2030; £10bn for munitions; back Trident and Ukraine; a new Veterans’ Bill.

- NHS and social care: Funding rises above inflation; 92,000 more nurses and 28,000 more doctors; Pharmacy First; 250 new/modernised GP surgeries; 50 more Community Diagnostic Centres; Dental Recovery Plan and NHS service commitment for new dentists; £3.4bn for NHS tech with the App as the single front door; cut 5,500 managers; women’s health action; smoke‑free generation bill; implement the Cass Review.

- Law, order and community safety: 8,000 more neighbourhood police (one for every ward); hotspot policing and community payback; Martyn’s Law; tougher sentences for serious offenders; new offences (spiking, deepfakes); relentless fraud crackdown.

- Standing up for communities and drivers: £20m endowment funds for 100+ towns; more Freeports and Investment Zones; Backing Drivers Bill to ban road pricing, reverse London’s ULEZ expansion, and require referendums for blanket 20mph/LTNs; £8.3bn for potholes; extend £2 bus fare cap for the whole Parliament.

- Homes in the right places: 1.6m homes with a brownfield fast‑track; unlock 100,000 by axing EU nutrient rules (with mitigation); protect the Green Belt; raise London densities; permanent Stamp Duty relief for first‑time buyers to £425,000; new Help to Buy; renters’ reform with fair evictions for ASB; finish leasehold reform; temporary CGT relief when landlords sell to tenants.

- Affordable, pragmatic net zero and energy security: Annual North Sea licensing; new gas plants to keep the lights on; treble offshore wind; approve two SMR fleets in the first 100 days; new nuclear at Wylfa; first CCS clusters; import carbon mechanism by 2027; lower green levies, no frequent‑flyer tax, no forced boiler rip‑and‑replace; stronger action on water companies; record flood defences; more trees and access to nature without a universal Right to Roam.

- Protecting women and girls and free speech: Clarify in law that sex means biological sex to safeguard single‑sex spaces and sport; align schools’ guidance on gender questioning; end private supply of puberty blockers; uphold press freedom and BBC impartiality.

- A strong Union, rural backing and food security: Protect the UK internal market; invest across Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland; increase UK‑wide farming budget by £1bn with a legal food security target; renew the £100m Seafood Fund; boost rural broadband, housing and services.

On 4 July, choose lower taxes, lower immigration, safer streets and protected pensions. Choose a secure future with the Conservatives.
